annotation.title_clean: Harnessing robot experimentation to optimize the regulatory framing of emerging robot technologies
annotation.title_en: Harnessing robot experimentation to optimize the regulatory framing of emerging robot technologies
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Calleja, C.; Drukarch, H.; Fosch-Villaronga, E.
annotation.summary_en: Article presents PROPELLING, a Horizon 2020 EUROBENCH project using robot testbeds to generate evidence for regulators. Using ISO 13482:2014 and lower-limb exoskeletons as a case study, it examines fear of falling, collision instability and protective stops, arguing experimentation can support evidence-based, better-informed robot standards and regulation.
key_provisions_or_claims: Information asymmetries between developers and regulators cause regulatory disconnection for emerging robots.
Robot testbeds can generate policy-relevant data to improve technical standards.
ISO 13482:2014 leaves gaps on fear of falling, collision instability and protective stops for exoskeletons.
PROPELLING proposes experiments to specify when protective stops should activate automatically.
Evidence-based approaches face challenges but can make robot policy more attuned to societal needs.
